section_title: Hearing and Building on Jesus’ Words

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 24 Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock. 25 The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

26 But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand. 27 The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and great was its collapse!”

context_lines: Jesus closes the Sermon's instruction with two people who hear the same words. The difference is what they do with them. One acts on His teaching, while the other hears without acting. The houses picture the different results.

Both houses face rain, rising water, and wind. The wise builder's house remains because its foundation is on rock. The foolish builder's house collapses because it rests on sand. The test exposes a difference that may not have been obvious before the storm.

The words to be acted on are Jesus' own words, including the teaching just given. The illustration gathers up the Sermon's call to righteousness in the heart, trust in the Father, mercy toward others, and an obedient response. Its place after the warning about judgment gives the collapse a serious final weight.

[Luke 6:46–49](https://biblehub.com/bsb/luke/6.htm) gives a closely related teaching about calling Jesus Lord, hearing Him, and acting on His words. [James 1:22–25](https://biblehub.com/bsb/james/1.htm) likewise warns that hearing without doing can become self-deception.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand the rock-and-sand picture as a call to put Jesus' teaching into practice, rather than being satisfied with hearing it. The [US Catholic bishops' notes on Matthew 7:24–27](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/matthew/7) emphasize this contrast between hearing and doing, and the Reformed [Westminster Confession, 16.2](https://www.opc.org/wcf.html), similarly describes obedience as the visible fruit of living faith.
god_plan_lines: Putting Jesus' words into practice becomes part of the mission of the risen Christ. In [Matthew 28:18–20](https://biblehub.com/bsb/matthew/28.htm), He sends His disciples to the nations and tells them to teach people to obey everything He commanded. He also promises His presence. The Sermon's call to act on His words continues within the people He gathers.

[Ephesians 2:8–10](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/2.htm) places a life of good works within God's work of making people new in Christ. This provides a wider setting for the image: the life built on His words is part of the life His grace creates.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
